title: Terrifying details emerge after caravan hijacked with children inside on Gold Coast hinterland
text:
7NEWS brings you the latest local news from Australia and around the world. Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS.
In a dramatic rescue, three young children were pulled through the roof of a caravan after it was allegedly stolen and crashed in front of their parents. Police allege a 59-year-old man illegally took the 1.
5-tonne caravan from the driveway of a home in the Gold Coast hinterland suburb of Tallai about 5.30pm on Tuesday. WATCH THE VIDEO ABOVE: Caravan allegedly hijacked with children inside. The man and the family are known to each other, Queensland Police Service said. 7NEWS understands the man leases the property and had reportedly been charging the family rent to park and live in their caravan on the driveway but the arrangement had recently broken down. A 40-year-old woman and her three children aged seven, five and two were inside the van, while her pet dog was underneath it, when the incident occurred. Police allege the man attached the caravan to the rear of his Nissan X-Trail station wagon using a single ratchet strap. The woman got out of the van before it was allegedly towed onto the road, injuring the dog. As the vehicle moved downhill, the caravan picked up speed, overtook the X-Trail and crashed into a ditch about 80m from the driveway, police said. It all allegedly happend in front of their horrified parents. Neighbours told 7NEWS it triggered panic on the street. “Yelling, screaming, kids crying, dogs yelping, all sorts,” neighbour Jack Hartigan said. “The whole street was down there — it was a big commotion.” The father climbed onto the caravan and pulled the children to safety through a skylight. “Dad hopped on top of the caravan and passed the kids out one-by-one,” neighbour Melissa Olivera told 7NEWS. The children were unharmed, but the dog suffered leg and head injuries. The family said their dog might lose a leg. The accused driver was taken to hospital as a precaution and has since been charged with unlawful use and dangerous operation of a motor vehicle. He was bailed to face Southport Magistrates Court on November 10. “I just planned to move the caravan from my property onto the nature strip in front,” the man later told 7NEWS. “I had no idea the kids were inside.” He claimed the situation spiralled out of control “because I was getting smashed in the face with a rock”. The family has since left the property and are staying with friends, and have said they plan to return to living in their caravan at a different location.
